## Escape analysis findings — how the silently-inert primary dedup guard survived every layer

All probes below ran in worktree `work-2399` (current `origin/main`, worktree `.venv`), read-only.
Input mechanism (from aa7b's root-cause pass): GUARD 3 of `_record_comment_id` fires on every
successful Cloud post because ACLI's batch mutation envelope carries no top-level `id`.

### AC1 — never-worked, not a regression (and the window was days, not months)

Probe: enumerate every revision of `.bridge_state/bindings.json` on `origin/tickets`
(`git log origin/tickets --format=%H --reverse -- .bridge_state/bindings.json` → **1011
revisions**), then `git show <rev>:.bridge_state/bindings.json` and count
`bindings` / `comment_ids` entries per revision (sampled every 50, then binary-searched the
transitions). Raw result:

| revision (tickets branch) | date | bindings | comment_ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1300f383c7 (first tracked) | 2026-08-06 | 1815 | key **absent** |
| 6685f723ae (rev 871) | 2026-08-15 01:58Z | ~2200 | key absent |
| 2e8003773e (rev 873) | 2026-08-15 15:16Z | ~2200 | key present, **0** |
| 67a71c8564 (rev 981) | 2026-08-20 06:47Z | ~2500 | **0** |
| 5c05bc1580 (rev 982) | 2026-08-21 04:37Z | ~2600 | **303** |
| 627c79cd59 (rev 1010, tip) | 2026-08-22 | 2612 | 625 |

The `comment_ids` key first appears 2026-08-15 — the first production pass after 789c's commit
27b868ba55e ("Append-only comment sync with comment-ID map") landed 2026-08-13. It holds **zero
entries in every revision** until the first pass after aa7b's fix 8d98c298fa8 ("Record mirrored
comments without a Jira id") landed 2026-08-20. **Verdict: never-worked** — the map was inert
from the feature's first production run to the fix. This also corrects this ticket's framing of
"months of production": the feature itself was ~6 days old when fixed; the escape window was
bounded by the feature's age, not by long-lived blindness. What WAS long-lived (Aug 6 tip
already shows 1815 bindings) is the duplicate symptom the inert guard permitted, remediated
separately (29,931 duplicates deleted, `darkish-enormous-raptors`).

### AC2 — test gap: each layer's tests seed the invariant the other layer establishes

Named pre-fix tests covering the dedup path (the fix added exactly ONE file,
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_comment_id_acli_envelope.py` — everything else predates
it): `apply/test_comment_id_capture.py` (apply-side recording),
`diffing/test_comment_id_map_diff.py` and `diffing/test_outbound_differ_comment_dedup.py`
(differ-side skips), `test_binding_store_comment_ids.py` (store unit),
`test_acli_comment_adf_encode.py` (transport encode).

Demonstration (the ticket's instrument): a pytest plugin (`escape_instrument_2399b.py`, quoted
below) that hard-wires `is_comment_mapped` to `False` on **every loaded copy** of
`BindingStore` (the suite loads reconciler modules as fresh per-test copies via
`spec_from_file_location`, so a single class patch misses them), run as:

```
PYTHONPATH=$PWD .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_outbound_differ_comment_dedup.py \
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_comment_id_map_diff.py \
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_comment_id_capture.py \
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_binding_store_comment_ids.py \
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_comment_adf_encode.py \
  -q -p escape_instrument_2399b
→ 5 failed, 26 passed
```

Reading the result honestly:

- The **26 passes** include every differ-level dedup test. Inspection shows why the instrument
  could not even reach them: `test_comment_id_map_diff.py` hands `_diff_comments` a private
  `_StubBindingStore` whose `is_comment_mapped` the test controls. The differ tests SEED the
  map state; the apply tests SEED the id-bearing response. **No test crosses the seam** (post →
  record → re-diff against the same store), so no test could observe that in production the
  seam never connects.
- The **5 failures** (`test_comment_id_capture.py` ×2, `test_binding_store_comment_ids.py` ×3)
  all directly assert `is_comment_mapped(...) is True` after feeding a **synthetic id-bearing
  payload** (`MagicMock` `{"id": "10001"}`). They fail under the instrument because they assert
  on the instrumented method itself — but they **passed for the entire escape window** while
  production was inert, because the defect lived UPSTREAM of what they stub: the real transport
  never produces an `id`. Per aa7b: no recorded real ACLI comment-create payload existed
  anywhere in the repo; the one test stubbing actual acli stdout hand-invents `'{"id": "10001"}'`.

So the characterisation is: the tests cover both shores of the dedup path and neither the
transport contract nor the seam between them — a test suite that would still pass with the
primary skip disabled end-to-end (and did, for the feature's whole life). The
fixture-provenance half of this gap is already owned by `crusty-brinish-ass`
(`3235-8aaf-e288-48f2`, filed from aa7b); the seam-crossing half is filed from this ticket
(below).

### AC3 — review gap: the criteria that existed abstain exactly on this class; the fix-side language landed post-escape

789c itself carries a signed `plan-review: PASS` attestation, so the gate ran. Criterion ids
checked against the current registry (`docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`, `rebar explain <id>`):

- **E4** (assumption/premise verification, blocking): probes CODEBASE assertions, and its
  discrimination rule explicitly **ABSTAINS-with-coverage on external-fact claims the tools
  cannot settle** ("the vendor already does Y"). 789c's fatal premise — the plan's "an unmapped
  key is created in Jira and **its returned ID recorded**" — is precisely that abstention class:
  a claim about an external CLI's response shape, unresolvable by Grep/Read of the repo.
- **T3** (integration feasibility, blocking): its EMPIRICISM DEPTH language (endpoint-surface
  granularity, four evidence classes) predates 789c (commits 0604f4ca469 / 3fc0a827b9f,
  2026-07-06) and still did not catch it, because its unit of analysis is whether named
  **subcommands/endpoints exist** — `acli` comment-create existed and was already called. What
  789c added was a new dependency on the **response schema** of an already-consumed endpoint, a
  unit T3's language does not name (and its ANTI-FP — "an internal, already-used integration is
  not-applicable" — points the reviewer away from it).
- **T2** (empirical probe, advisory) lists "an unverified assumption about an external system"
  as a trigger — at best an advisory recommendation of a spike, not a block.
- **T5b** (reliability overlay, advisory): "error states are surfaced, not swallowed" is
  on-point for the silent `return`, but it is advisory, plan-level, and the guard was a code
  detail no plan sentence described.
- **Code review**: at 789c's review (2026-08-13) **no dimension addressed fail-open /
  silently-inert guards**. On 2026-08-21 — after this escape, as one of "nine recorded
  instances in one session" — commit 4c57247ff88 added fail-open check detection to the two
  existing hosts (`code-review-tests`, `code-review-base` `error-handling`), with the
  producer-liveness litmus that names this exact shape ("a check whose PASS/absent/empty result
  is indistinguishable from the check never having run"), **per an operator ruling of "no new
  criterion"**. The code-review-side gap is therefore already closed, by the operator's chosen
  mechanism; this analysis proposes no criterion change (and respects the standing rejection of
  CI-coupled criteria).

Summary: the guard escaped review not because reviewers were careless but because every
blocking criterion's scope boundary was drawn just short of it — E4 abstains on external facts,
T3 stops at endpoint existence, T5b sees plans rather than guards — and the one rubric that
names the shape did not exist yet.

### AC4 — portable detection proposal (filed, not implemented)

The layer still uncovered after 4c57247ff88 is **production observability**: the invariant
violation (`comment_ids == 0` while `bindings` grew past 2,475 and outbound comment posts kept
succeeding) sat in committed production data for the feature's whole life with no reader. A
review-time rubric cannot see production state; this needs an operation-linked check.

Proposal (filed as its own ticket, linked `discovered_from`): an **in-process reconciler
invariant** — at end-of-pass summary (or binding-store save), if this pass successfully posted
outbound comments and `comment_ids` gained no entries, emit a loud signal through the existing
`bridge_alerts` machinery (already part of the reduced ticket state). Operation-linked, runs
wherever the reconciler runs, no CI trigger — satisfying `project.portability` by construction.
Cost: a counter and a comparison per pass. This is a code proposal, not a gate/criterion
change; adjudication of whether it is worth even that cost stays with the ticket.

Second filed ticket: a **seam-crossing dedup test** — drive the real apply-phase recording with
the transport's REAL envelope shape (the fixture 8d98c298fa8 added), then re-run
`_diff_comments` against the SAME store instance and assert the skip engages — closing the
"each layer seeds the other's invariant" hole that the instrument run demonstrated. Distinct
from `crusty-brinish-ass` (fixture provenance for the transport) — this one tests the seam.

### Instrument (for reproducibility)

```python
# escape_instrument_2399b.py — pytest plugin (-p escape_instrument_2399b)
import sys, pytest

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _disable_primary_dedup_skip(monkeypatch):
    for name, mod in list(sys.modules.items()):
        bs = getattr(mod, "BindingStore", None)
        if bs is not None and hasattr(bs, "is_comment_mapped"):
            monkeypatch.setattr(bs, "is_comment_mapped", lambda self, key: False)
    yield
```
